html:
SMTO-EXE-0228 — Docker Compose isn't working on the Gateway computer

GUID: f7534b3e-c4a7-5156-bf3c-d3054197b1d8
Slug: docker-compose-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO needs Docker Compose, the Docker add-on that starts groups of containers together, on the Gateway computer. It's missing or didn't answer correctly there, so no Compose action ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to make sure Docker and its Compose add-on are installed for the account the Gateway runs as. SMTO looks for Docker in that account's setup and checks that Compose answers.
  2. Have them rerun the Gateway installer on that computer as the Gateway's account, for example ./install.sh from the SMTO folder, to repair it in place. On most Linux computers the installer adds missing Docker tools, including Compose, and repairs the Gateway without removing its setup.
  3. When no tasks are running there, restart the Gateway program. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. The Gateway only reports Compose as available after it restarts and finds a working Compose.
  4. Start a new task for your Compose request. An existing task keeps the list of Gateway abilities it saw when it started.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds, and a new task runs your Compose request without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed the Gateway. Repair it in place: don't delete the Gateway's pairing, sign-ins, settings or task files. Turning on the Docker skill's permission doesn't install Compose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not find the docker CLI on its PATH, or the Compose readiness check (docker compose version --format json) failed, so the Compose capability is unavailable.

What this means

  • Docker CLI/Compose discovery could not find the executable or its bounded version/readiness check failed the supported Compose plugin contract. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Docker CLI/Compose discovery could not find the executable or its bounded version/readiness check failed the supported Compose plugin contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway account's CLI path and Compose readiness/version, distinguishing missing software from failed execution.

How to fix it

  • As the Gateway account on that host, run docker compose version; install or repair the Docker CLI and Compose v2 plugin, or rerun ./install.sh (or ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS) in place without deleting pairing, credentials or state. After active work settles, restart the Gateway, refresh its metadata, confirm docker_compose is advertised, and start a new task.
  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported Compose plugin passes readiness under the Gateway account.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
